<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md -->

# Packages

kernl publishes four packages under the `@kernl` scope. Three are pure contracts and engines with zero framework dependencies; one composes them with kehto and applesauce. The shell app at `apps/web` is not published.

| Package | Version | Role | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`@kernl/guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/guard.md) | `0.1.0` | Ingress flood control, visibility gate, focus-aware firewall, CSP profile, mitigation descriptions. | `@kehto/firewall` |
| [`@kernl/messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/messaging.md) | `0.1.0` | Messaging provider contract, registry, composite direct-message adapter. | `@napplet/core` (types, peer) |
| [`@kernl/bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/bridges.md) | `0.1.0` | Locator parsing, bridge contract, registry, HTTP bridge with SSRF policy. | nothing |
| [`@kernl/core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/core.md) | `0.1.0` | Composition root over kehto and applesauce: adapters, applet resolution, mount plan, consent summaries, layouts, persistence. | the three above, `@kehto/*`, `applesauce-*`, `rxjs` |

## Shared rules

- ESM only, TypeScript strict, `verbatimModuleSyntax`. Each package ships `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` with `sideEffects: false`.
- Every public export has JSDoc with `@param`, `@returns` and `@example`, and appears in the [API reference](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md).
- Subscriptions return `{ close() }`. Errors carry a stable prefixed reason: `denied:`, `invalid:`, `unavailable:`.
- No published package imports `nostr-tools` directly, and no published package depends on a UI framework. `pnpm check:deps` enforces both.
- Behaviour is specified in Gherkin under each package's `features/` and run by vitest with 100% coverage over `src`.

## Versioning

All packages are `0.x`. A breaking change is a `minor` bump; everything else is a `patch`. Releases are managed with changesets: one changeset per package whose shipped output changed. `@kernl/core` depends on the other three with `workspace:^`, so a release of a leaf package produces a patch of core.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @kernl/core
# or individually
pnpm add @kernl/guard @kernl/messaging @kernl/bridges
```

`@kernl/core` pulls the other three in. Install a leaf package alone when you want its contract without kehto and applesauce, for example `@kernl/guard` to test an applet against the limits, or `@kernl/messaging` to write a provider.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/messaging.md -->

# @kernl/messaging

Messaging provider contract, registry, composite direct-message backend and an in-memory backend for the kernl shell. Pure: no relay code, no signer, no kehto dependency. Providers receive their backend constructor from the shell.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `@kernl/messaging` |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Entry | `./dist/index.js`, types `./dist/index.d.ts` |
| Dependencies | none |
| Peer dependencies | `@napplet/core >=0.37.0 <0.38.0` (the `Dm*` wire types) |
| Side effects | none |

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @kernl/messaging
```

## Purpose

One contract for every private-messaging protocol, truthful self-description instead of ranking, and one composite backend that projects every enabled provider onto the NAP `dm` domain. The concepts are in [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md); the opinion is D-009.

## Exports

### Contract

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MessagingProvider` | interface | `{ id; name; description; properties: SecurityProperties; availability(): ProviderAvailability; createBackend(): MessagingBackend }`. `id` is the conversation-id prefix. |
| `MessagingBackend` | interface | `status()`, `conversations(query?)`, `messages(query)`, `send(request)`, `subscribe(request, onMessage)`, `unsubscribe(subscriptionId)`, `close?()`. Every method except `send` may return synchronously or a promise. Structurally kehto's `DmAdapter`. |
| `SecurityProperties` | interface | `forwardSecrecy`, `postCompromiseSecurity`, `metadataProtection: 'none' \| 'partial' \| 'strong'`, `requiresSameClient`, `groups`, `specification?`, `experimental`. |
| `ProviderAvailability` | union | `{ available: true }` or `{ available: false; reason: string }`. The reason is a bare word such as `signed-out`; the registry prefixes it as `unavailable:<reason>`. |
| `ProviderEntry` | interface | `{ provider; enabled: boolean; availability: ProviderAvailability }`, what `MessagingRegistry.list()` and `get()` return. |
| `MessagingPreferences` | interface | `{ enabled: readonly string[]; defaultProvider?: string }`, the persisted registry state. |
| `PACKAGE_NAME` | `'@kernl/messaging'` | The package name as a constant. |

### Registry

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMessagingRegistry` | `(options?: MessagingRegistryOptions) => MessagingRegistry` | One per shell. Owns one backend per enabled provider, restores saved preferences lazily as providers register, and hands out one stable composite backend. |
| `MessagingRegistryOptions` | interface | `{ preferences?: MessagingPreferences; onChange?: (preferences: MessagingPreferences) => void }`. `onChange` receives a frozen snapshot after every change. |
| `MessagingRegistry` | interface | `register(provider)`, `list()`, `get(id)`, `enable(id)`, `disable(id)`, `setDefault(id)`, `preferences()`, `composite()`, `close()`. Error reasons: `invalid:duplicate-provider`, `invalid:unknown-provider`, `unavailable:<reason>`, `invalid:provider-not-enabled`. |

### Composite backend

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createCompositeBackend` | `(resolveEnabled: () => readonly EnabledBackend[], getDefault: () => string \| undefined) => MessagingBackend` | One backend over every enabled provider. Ids leaving it are `<providerId>:<innerId>`; ids arriving are routed by prefix. Rules for cursors, sends and subscriptions are in [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md#the-composite-backend). |
| `EnabledBackend` | interface | `{ id: string; backend: MessagingBackend }`. |
| `WithProvider<T>` | type | `T & { provider?: string }`: a `DmSendRequest` that names the provider for a new conversation. |
| `namespaceId` | `(providerId: string, innerId: string) => string` | `'private:direct:ab,cd'`. |
| `splitId` | `(id: string) => NamespacedId \| undefined` | Splits on the first `:`; `undefined` when there is no prefix. |
| `NamespacedId` | interface | `{ providerId: string; innerId: string }`. |

### In-memory backend

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMemoryBackend` | `(options?: MemoryBackendOptions) => MemoryBackend` | A complete backend in memory for tests and the shell's offline preview. Conversations are keyed `direct:<pubkey>` or `group:<pubkey>,<pubkey>` over the sorted correspondents; cursors are numeric offsets; unread is the count of `received` messages. |
| `MemoryBackendOptions` | interface | `{ owner?: string (default 'owner'); available?: boolean (default true); now?: () => number }`. `now` is in Unix seconds and defaults to the wall clock. |
| `MemoryBackend` | interface | `MessagingBackend` plus `deliver(incoming: MemoryIncoming): DmMessage` (stores a `received` message and notifies matching subscribers) and a non-optional `close()` that drops every subscriber. |
| `MemoryIncoming` | interface | `{ senderPubkey; content; conversationId?; createdAt? }`. Without `conversationId` the message lands in `direct:<senderPubkey>`. |

`send()` rejects with `invalid:no-recipients` when neither a conversation nor a recipient other than the owner is named, `invalid:unknown-conversation` for an id the backend has never seen, and `unavailable:offline` while `available` is false. Reads keep working offline.

### Providers

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createPrivateMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `private`, name "Private messages". NIP-17. |
| `createLegacyMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `legacy`, name "Legacy messages". NIP-04. |
| `createRatchetMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `ratchet`, name "Ratchet sessions". nostr-double-ratchet draft; `experimental: true`. |
| `defineProvider` | `(definition: ProviderDefinition, deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Joins fixed copy and properties with the shell's backend constructor and availability check. The three built-ins are made with it. |
| `ProviderDeps` | interface | `{ createBackend: () => MessagingBackend; available: () => ProviderAvailability }`. |
| `ProviderDefinition` | interface | `{ id; name; description; properties: SecurityProperties }`. |
| `describeProvider` | `(provider: MessagingProvider) => readonly ProviderDescriptionRow[]` | Six label/value rows for the picker, in a fixed order; `specification` is left out so no protocol name reaches the UI. |
| `ProviderDescriptionRow` | interface | `{ label: string; value: string }`. |

## Example

```ts
import { createCompositeBackend, createMemoryBackend, createMessagingRegistry, createPrivateMessagesProvider } from '@kernl/messaging';

const backend = createMemoryBackend({ owner: 'me', now: () => 1_700_000_000 });
await backend.send({ recipients: ['alice'], content: 'hi' });
backend.deliver({ senderPubkey: 'alice', content: 'hello' });

const registry = createMessagingRegistry({ onChange: (prefs) => console.log(prefs) });
registry.register(createPrivateMessagesProvider({ createBackend: () => backend, available: () => ({ available: true }) }));
registry.enable('private');
registry.setDefault('private');

const page = await registry.composite().conversations({ limit: 20 });
page.conversations[0]?.id; // 'private:direct:alice'

// the same composite, assembled by hand
createCompositeBackend(() => [{ id: 'private', backend }], () => 'private');
```

## Scope

- Holds no relay, store or signer. The shell passes a `createBackend` function; what it closes over is the shell's business.
- Does not rank, score or recommend. `SecurityProperties` is rendered verbatim by `describeProvider`.
- Does not translate wire types; `@napplet/core`'s `Dm*` types are used directly.
- Owns backend lifetimes through the registry. The composite's `close()` is a no-op by design.

## Specification

`packages/messaging/features/`: `registry.feature`, `composite.feature`, `memory-backend.feature`, `providers.feature`.

## API reference

Generated module: [`_kernl_messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_messaging.html)

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/index.md -->

# Policies

Rules the repository enforces mechanically. Each policy names the script that checks it and the decision in `DECISIONS.md` that motivates it. A policy that cannot be checked by a script is a convention, and conventions live in `AGENTS.md`, not here.

| Policy | Checked by | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Public vocabulary](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md) | `pnpm check:vocabulary` (`scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs`) | D-006 |
| [Security posture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/security-posture.md) | `features/` scenarios, `pnpm check:deps`, Playwright in `pnpm test:e2e` | D-001, D-002, D-003 |
| [Spec conformance](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md) | `@napplet/conformance` in the test suite; review | `AGENTS.md` "Spec before code" |

Two further gates apply to everything, including these pages:

- **Docs gate.** `pnpm docs:check` builds TypeDoc and VitePress, then runs `scripts/audit-docs.mjs`: a page per package with its version row, every page in the sidebar, a TypeDoc module per package, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a Markdown twin per built page.
- **Slop gate.** `pnpm slop` runs aislop over the repository and `scripts/assert-slop-score.mjs` fails below 100. Functions under 120 lines, files under 600, nesting under 4, at most 5 parameters, no narrative comments.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md -->

# Public vocabulary

The public website and the shell UI never name a protocol. The person is the point; the protocol is plumbing. This page is the denylist, the reasoning, and where the rule stops.

## The rule

`scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs` scans the built output of `apps/web` (the landing pages and the shell's UI copy) and fails the build on any of these, case-insensitively, as whole words or prefixes where marked:

| Denied | Say instead |
| --- | --- |
| `nostr` | "your account", "the network" |
| `nip-` (prefix) | describe the behaviour: "signing extension", "remote signer", "private messages" |
| `napplet` | "applet" |
| `relay` | "network", or nothing: the user's relays are "where your account lives" |
| `pubkey` | "account", "address" |
| `npub` | "address" |
| `nsec` | "secret key", in the one place the shell must warn about it |

Two checks enforce it:

- **Build time.** `scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs` reads every HTML, Markdown, text, JSON and XML file in the Pages artifact outside `docs/`, so Astro pages, JSON-LD, `llms.txt` and the Markdown twins are covered.
- **In a browser.** `tests/e2e/public-vocabulary.spec.ts` loads every public page and walks the shell (sign-in, launcher, applet summary, a running applet's frame, the consent dialog with its record view open, and the guard, messages, grants and settings panels). It reads what a person can perceive: rendered text, `title`, `aria-label`, `placeholder` and `alt`. Copy rendered by scripts, which the file scan cannot see, is covered here.

Identifiers inside JavaScript bundles are not copy and are not checked. The consent dialog's record view shows every field of the event it will sign, with plain labels ("Signed by", "Type", "Labels") instead of wire field names.

## Why

Three reasons, in the order `SOUL.md` ranks them.

**The user's agency.** A person deciding whether to run an applet needs to know what it will do and what it can reach. A protocol name tells them nothing about either; it tells them which club they are supposed to already belong to. "This applet wants to publish on your behalf" is a decision a person can make. "This applet requires `relay` and `outbox`" is not.

**Protocol conformance is a property of the code, not the copy.** kernl conforms to NIP-5D and the NAPs, and the docs say so precisely. Saying so on the landing page would not make the code conform more; it would make the page about the specification instead of about what a person can do.

**Providers and bridges are chosen by what they do.** A user chooses a messaging provider by whether their correspondent can read it and what an observer learns, not by its wire format. A bridge is "downloads", not the name of a peer-to-peer protocol. Naming protocols in the UI would invite ranking by familiarity, which D-009 and D-010 rule out.

## Where the rule stops

- **These docs.** Written for developers, who need the names. Every page here uses them.
- **Code, specs, commit messages, issues.** `napplet` is the protocol term and stays in identifiers and in `features/`.
- **`specification` fields.** `SecurityProperties.specification` and a bridge's protocol are shown in the docs, never in the picker.
- **Addresses.** Server URLs a user adds, edits or removes are data, and their hostnames belong to whoever runs the server. Both checks ignore `http(s)://` and `ws(s)://` URLs.
- **The secret-key warning.** The one place the shell mentions `nsec` is the warning that it will never ask for one.

## The words we use

| Say | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| applet | napplet, app, dapp | "napplet" remains the protocol term in code and specs. |
| shell | OS, desktop, browser | kernl runs in a browser; it is not one. |
| grant | permission, capability | A grant is something the user gave and can take back. |
| provider | protocol | Users choose providers by what they do. |
| guard | firewall, mitigation | The guard is the set of protections between an applet and the user. |

Marketing adjectives, filler and hedges that hide a decision are out everywhere, including here.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/security-posture.md -->

# Security posture

The rules the shell keeps when it runs untrusted code next to the user's identity. Each rule has a scenario in `features/` or a check in `scripts/`; a rule with neither is a wish.

## Mount rules

1. **`srcdoc`, never `src`.** The applet document is the verified bytes with the shell prelude and CSP injected outside the signed content. A `src` URL would give the applet an origin and a network path the shell does not mediate.
2. **`sandbox="allow-scripts"` only.** Never `allow-same-origin`, never `allow-top-navigation`, never `allow-popups`. The frame has an opaque origin and cannot reach the shell's storage or DOM.
3. **The guard's CSP, unchanged by profile.** `createAppletCsp(profile)` is applied through `prepareNappletSrcdoc`; it returns the same policy for every profile. No grant, profile or setting alters it. See [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#why-csp-never-loosens).
4. **`denyNappletControllerAccess(frame)`** before the frame is attached, so the applet cannot reach a service worker or controller the shell registered.
5. **Order: register → set environment → observe frame → assign `srcdoc`.** `originRegistry.register(contentWindow, windowId, identity)`, then `originRegistry.setEnvironment(contentWindow, environment)`, then `bridge.observeFrame(frame, windowId)`, then `frame.srcdoc = plan.srcdoc`. Assigning `srcdoc` first would let the document's first message arrive before the shell knows who it is.
6. **Remove the iframe on every revocation reason.** `window-message`, `second-hello`, `invalid-hello`, `second-load`, `port-closed` and `host` all end with the frame gone and the guard's state for the window forgotten. A revoked window's identity is never re-bound to the same frame.

## Identity rules

7. **Verified bytes come from `@kehto/nip/5d` `resolveNapplet`.** Gateways and caches are accelerators; the hash is the identity. Cached bytes are re-verified on every read.
8. **Identity is `(dTag, artifactHash)` plus one port.** Grants are keyed by that identity; a new build is a new identity with no grants.
9. **Restrictive by narrowing.** `resolveEnvironment` returns only granted domains; kehto intersects, so the hook can only remove. The runtime's permissive default is never reached for an ungranted domain.

## Key rules

10. **Keys live only inside applesauce signer instances.** `ExtensionSigner`, `NostrConnectSigner`, `PasswordAccount`'s wrapped signer. kernl never holds raw key bytes and never serialises a private key outside `PasswordAccount`.
11. **Applets never see `window.nostr`.** The sandbox has no extension injection, and the shell does not forward one.
12. **Every signature the applet asks for goes through consent or an existing grant**, and destructive kinds (0, 3, 5, 10002) are shown as semantic diffs before signing.

## Network rules

13. **No applet network path exists outside the shell.** All bytes arrive through the `resource` domain and a bridge. The HTTP bridge enforces `https` only, 3 redirects, 10 MiB, 20 s and a private-address block re-checked on every hop.
14. **One `RelayPool`.** No service, provider or bridge opens its own connection. Adapters over the shared pool satisfy kehto's contracts.
15. **Hidden windows are deferred, not served.** The visibility gate holds their traffic; the hidden resource allowance caps their requests.

## Log rules

16. **Secrets never appear in logs, guard events or consent summaries.** `GuardEvent.reason` is a stable prefixed string; `NappletRevocation.detail` never includes message payloads; `describeChange` output names fields, not key material.
17. **Guard events are shown to the user**, with the applet and the reason. They are not sent anywhere.

## Dependency rules

18. **`nostr-tools` is never imported by kernl source.** It is a transitive peer of kehto and applesauce only.
19. **Published packages have zero framework dependencies.** `svelte`, `react`, `vue`, `preact`, `solid-js` and `lit` are forbidden in every `packages/*/package.json`.
20. **Leaf packages do not import `@kehto/*`**, except `@kernl/guard`, which imports `@kehto/firewall`. Only `@kernl/core` composes kehto.

Rules 18 to 20 are enforced by `scripts/check-dependency-rules.mjs` (`pnpm check:deps`). Rules 1 to 17 are scenarios in `packages/*/features/` and `features/`, and the mount rules are additionally exercised in the browser by the Playwright suite.

## Reporting

A posture violation is a bug of the highest severity in this repository, above any feature. Report it as an issue on `kernlize/web` with the rule number. If it involves a kehto seam, the issue is filed upstream too, and `DECISIONS.md` records the gap.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md -->

# Spec conformance

kernl conforms to specifications it does not own. This page says which ones, what "upstream first" means in practice, and how a gap is recorded.

## Authority

| Area | Authority | Local copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell–applet protocol | NIP-5D, [nostr-protocol/nips PR #2303](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/pull/2303) | none |
| NAP domains (`relay`, `outbox`, `dm`, `resource`, …) | [napplet/naps](https://github.com/napplet/naps) | none |
| Wire types and dispatch | [`@napplet/core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@napplet/core), pinned `>=0.37.0 <0.38.0` | the installed package |
| Shell composition | kehto source, `@kehto/*` at the pinned ranges | the installed packages |
| Event layer | applesauce v7, [applesauce.build](https://applesauce.build) | the installed packages |
| Messaging protocols | NIP-17, NIP-04, the nostr double-ratchet draft, as named in each provider's `specification` | none |

kernl keeps no local copy of a specification text. A copy drifts; a link does not. When the PR or a NAP document changes, the behaviour changes in kernl in a pull request that cites the clause.

## Upstream first

When kernl needs something a specification or an upstream package does not provide, the order is:

1. **Compose it from what exists.** Most of kernl is this: the guard composes `@kehto/firewall`'s `evaluate()`, the restrictive posture composes `resolveEnvironment` and `aclState.grant`.
2. **Propose it upstream.** An issue or pull request on `kehto/web`, `napplet/naps` or `nostr-protocol/nips`, as appropriate. The four open kehto proposals are in [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).
3. **Implement it locally with a recorded gap.** Only when 1 is impossible and 2 is pending. The local implementation sits behind an interface, cites the upstream issue, and is removed when upstream lands.

kernl never re-implements a kehto primitive because it was easier than reading kehto's source, and never invents wire format. When a NAP is ambiguous, kernl prefers an upstream issue over a guess and records the ambiguity next to the code.

## What conformance is checked by

- **`@napplet/conformance`** runs in the test suite against the shell's bridge: envelope validators per NAP domain, manifest validation and the reference mock shell's expectations of a host.
- **Gherkin scenarios** in `features/` for every protocol-visible behaviour, named after the clause they implement where one exists.
- **Review.** A change that touches an envelope shape, a domain's semantics or the handshake cites the clause in its description. A reviewer checks the clause, not the summary.

The docs are non-normative. Where a page here and the specification disagree, the specification wins and the page has a bug.

## Recording a gap

A gap is anything kernl does that the specification does not say, or does not do that the specification says. Record it in three places:

1. **Next to the code**, as a comment that names the clause and the upstream issue. This is one of the few comments the slop gate accepts, because a reader could not infer it.
2. **In `DECISIONS.md`**, as a `D-NNN` entry with Context, Decision, Consequences and Reversal cost. If the gap is a kehto seam, the entry says what upstream change would close it.
3. **In [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md)**, under upstream gaps, so a reader deciding whether to depend on kernl sees it without reading the decisions log.

A gap closes when upstream lands and the local layer is deleted. The `DECISIONS.md` entry stays, with a `Superseded by` line.

## Tie-breaking

Protocol conformance is second in `SOUL.md`'s tie-breakers, below the user's safety and agency and above the applet developer's ability to build. A conformance requirement that would weaken the user's position is not implemented silently; it is raised upstream with the conflict stated, and `DECISIONS.md` records which way kernl went while the question is open.

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md -->

# API reference

The API reference is generated from source JSDoc by TypeDoc 0.28 with `entryPointStrategy: packages` over the four workspaces in `typedoc.json`. It is written to `docs/api/` and served next to this site at `/docs/api/`.

```bash
pnpm docs:api
```

Do not edit the generated files. Fix the JSDoc in `packages/*/src` and rerun. `treatWarningsAsErrors` is on, so an export without documentation, a broken `{@link}` or a missing git remote fails the build.

## Modules

| Package | Module page |
| --- | --- |
| `@kernl/guard` | [`_kernl_guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_guard.html) |
| `@kernl/messaging` | [`_kernl_messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_messaging.html) |
| `@kernl/bridges` | [`_kernl_bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_bridges.html) |
| `@kernl/core` | [`_kernl_core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_core.html) |

The [index page](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/index.html) lists all four, and the [hierarchy page](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/hierarchy.html) shows type relationships across them.

## How to read it

- Each module page lists its exports by kind: interfaces, type aliases, functions, variables. Every entry has at least one `@example`.
- Reasons in thrown errors are documented as string literals (`denied:…`, `invalid:…`, `unavailable:…`) on the function that throws them.
- Types imported from `@kehto/*` or `@napplet/core` are linked to their names but not expanded; `excludeExternals` keeps the reference to kernl's own surface.
- The reference is HTML only. It has no Markdown twin and is not included in `llms-full.txt`; the [package pages](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md) carry the export lists in Markdown for agents.

## Audit

`scripts/audit-docs.mjs` asserts that `docs/api/modules/_kernl_<package>.html` exists for every `packages/*/package.json`, that each package page links to it, and that the built docs carry their Markdown twins. It runs as part of `pnpm docs:check`.

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/roadmap.md -->

# Roadmap

Ordered by the tie-breakers in `SOUL.md`: the user's safety and agency first, protocol conformance second, the applet developer's ability to build third. Nothing here is dated. An item moves off this page when its scenarios pass and its docs exist.

## 1. Upstream pull requests to kehto

Each item shrinks kernl when it lands; see [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).

- Forward `getFocusContext`, `onFirewallEvent` and `firewallPersistence` through `ShellAdapter` so the runtime's own firewall can be focus-aware without a second engine in front of it.
- Let the host choose the ACL default policy in `createRuntime`, so a restrictive shell does not have to write every capability explicitly.
- Offer a pre-dispatch hook on port traffic, so the visibility gate can hold a hidden applet's envelopes instead of observing them after dispatch.
- Expose a setter for the runtime firewall's `unfocusedMultiplier`, so the profile's focus tightening applies before dispatch as well as after.

## 2. Bridge backends

Each backend plugs into the path the HTTP bridge already exercises end to end. Order reflects how much of the user's exposure each one changes; see [Bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md).

| Backend | Interface | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mail | `MailBackend` | Opens or creates a conversation for a `mailto:` locator. Candidate for a shell-side IMAP/JMAP client or a hand-off to a configured mail account. |
| NZB | `NzbBackend` | Hands an `nzb:` locator to a configured downloader. The downloader runs outside the browser; the bridge reports job state. |
| Torrent | `TorrentBackend` | Adds an info hash with its trackers. WebTorrent in the shell, or a configured external client. Marked as public activity in the exposure description. |
| Soulseek | `SoulseekBackend` | Requests one file from one peer. Requires a daemon; the bridge reports job state. |

## 3. Messaging

- Supply the double-ratchet runtime so the `ratchet` provider reports `available`. Its properties are already described; see [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md).
- Per-conversation provider migration: move a correspondent from `legacy` to `private` when both clients can read it, shown as a reversible choice.

## 4. Mobile layouts

The window manager contracts come from `@kehto/wm`. A narrow-viewport layout with a window switcher, gestures for focus and dismissal, and the same visibility semantics the guard relies on (a window off screen is hidden, and hidden windows are deferred).

## 5. Account switching

`AccountManager` already holds several accounts. The missing piece is a switcher that makes the active account visible on every screen, keeps grants scoped to the account that gave them, and never signs a write with an account the user did not pick for that window.

## 6. Guard

- Per-applet guard profiles: today the profile is shell-wide and resets to `strict` on boot (D-003). Next: an override per applet identity, remembered locally.
- Re-narrow a live applet's advertised environment when a domain is revoked; today the ACL denies at once but `shell.init` only changes on the next open.
- Bridge consent per host: wire `createDefaultBridges({ authorize })` to a host prompt so a granted `resource` request still asks before reaching a new origin.
- Persist per-applet profile overrides and grants through a user-chosen sync, so loosening an applet once does not have to be repeated per device.
- A readable guard log in the shell: every `defer`, `reject`, `quarantine` and `flag` event, with the stable reason and the applet it concerned.

## Not planned

- A global configuration flag that loosens a mitigation for every applet. `SOUL.md` opinion three rules it out.
- A second event library beside applesauce. `DECISIONS.md` D-002 rules it out.
- A "recommended" messaging provider. D-009 rules it out.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/build-an-applet-for-kernl.md -->

# Build an applet for kernl

kernl adds nothing to the applet format. An applet that conforms to NIP-5D and the NAPs runs in kernl. What kernl changes is the posture the applet meets: fewer domains until granted, deferral while hidden, limits that tighten when the window loses focus. This page tells you what to expect and how to test for it.

## Use the applet SDK, not this repository

The applet side of the protocol is maintained at [napplet.run](https://napplet.run/docs/). Start there:

- [`@napplet/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@napplet/sdk) gives you typed named exports over `window.napplet` for bundler-based projects.
- [`@napplet/conformance`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@napplet/conformance) is the framework-agnostic conformance engine: a reference mock shell, per-NAP envelope validators, a manifest validator and reporters. `@napplet/conformance-cli` runs it from the command line.
- The [napplet.run getting-started guide](https://napplet.run/docs/guide/getting-started.html) and the [NAP documents](https://github.com/napplet/naps) are the authority on wire format and domain semantics.

kernl's packages are shell-side. You do not import them in an applet.

## What kernl advertises

`shell.ready` tells your applet which domains this shell offers for your identity. In kernl that set is narrowed per applet by the user's grants (see [Identity and grants](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/identity-and-grants.md)), so read it rather than assuming. The draft's intended advertisement:

| Posture | Domains | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Advertised without a grant | `shell`, `theme`, `config` | Read-only shell state. Always present. |
| Advertised once granted; may appear in `requires` (**R**) | `identity`, `relay`, `outbox`, `keys`, `storage`, `resource`, `lists`, `dm` | The user is asked at mount time for each of these you require. |
| Advertised only when the shell has a backend; optional only (**O**) | `notify`, `media`, `intent`, `link`, `upload` | Never satisfy `requires`. Check `shell.ready` and degrade. |
| Not advertised in this draft | `cvm`, `llm`, `ble`, `webrtc`, `serial`, `fs`, `gamepad`, `inc`, `count` | Requiring one of these means your applet does not mount in kernl. |

Put a domain in `requires` only if your applet is useless without it. Every required domain is one more thing the user must agree to before seeing anything, and a user who declines sees nothing. Prefer `optional` and a graceful fallback.

## What the strict profile means for you

The shell boots every applet in `strict`. The numbers are in [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#profiles); the behaviours you will notice:

**Deferral when hidden.** When your window is minimised or on an inactive workspace, every envelope except `control` traffic (`shell.*`, `theme.*`, `identity.*`, `relay.close`, `storage.get`, …) is held, not dispatched, and released oldest first when the window is visible again. Your `await` resolves late, not with an error. Design for it: do not time out a request after a few seconds, and do not assume a subscription delivers while you are hidden. Up to 200 envelopes are held; the 201st is rejected with `defer:queue-full`.

**Hidden resource allowance.** A hidden window may make 8 `resource.*` requests; the ninth quarantines the window with `flood:hidden-resource` until the user releases it. The count resets as soon as the window is visible again. Fetch what you need while visible.

**Rate limits by operation class.** Each class has its own token bucket, keyed by your applet's `dTag`, so two windows of your applet share one budget. In `strict`: 30 `relay.subscribe` and 20 `relay.publish` per minute, 5 deletions (kind 5) per minute, 20 `dm.send` and 10 `intent.*` per minute, 120 `resource.*` and 60 `storage.set`/`storage.remove` per 10 seconds. While your window is not focused, capacity is multiplied by 0.25. A rejected envelope carries a stable reason such as `rate:relay:publish`.

**Ingress flood control.** Each window may send 8 messages per second; the ninth inside the same second is queued (`flood:burst`) and released as the budget refills, `control` and `resource.*` envelopes first. Once 64 messages are queued, further ones are rejected with `flood:queue-full`; 300 messages inside any rolling 10 seconds quarantines the window with `flood:quarantine` until the user intervenes. Batch your writes and coalesce your subscriptions.

**Envelope caps.** `resource.*` envelopes over 64 KiB and `relay.subscribe`/`outbox.subscribe` (including `outbox.query`) envelopes over 256 KiB are rejected with `size:<class>` before parsing. Large filters are a smell; split them.

**No init-burst exemption.** kehto's own init-burst guard is not what runs here: kernl enforces the same 8 messages per second from the first message your applet sends. Load lazily: request the first screen, render, then fetch the rest.

**Consent for destructive kinds.** Publishing kind 0, 3, 5 or 10002 shows the user a diff of what changes and waits. Expect the publish to take as long as a person takes to read, and expect `denied:` if they refuse.

None of this changes the wire format. A rejection is a normal NAP error envelope with a reason string; a deferral is latency.

## Test against the guard

You can exercise the guard without the full shell. `@kernl/guard` is pure, and the mock shell in `@napplet/conformance` can be wrapped with it:

```ts
import { createGuardConfig, createIngressGuard, createVisibilityGate, type GuardEvent } from '@kernl/guard';

const events: GuardEvent[] = [];
const config = createGuardConfig('strict');
const guard = createIngressGuard({ config, onEvent: (event) => events.push(event) });
const gate = createVisibilityGate({ config, onEvent: (event) => events.push(event) });

gate.setVisibility('w1', { visible: false, focused: false });
if (gate.shouldDefer('w1', 'relay:subscribe')) gate.defer('w1', { type: 'relay.subscribe', size: 512 });
// held; gate.drain('w1') returns it once the window is visible again

gate.setVisibility('w1', { visible: true, focused: true });
for (let i = 0; i < 9; i += 1) {
  guard.admit('w1', 'my-applet', { type: 'relay.publish', kind: 1 }, gate.getVisibility('w1'));
}
// the ninth call inside one second returns 'defer' and emits { disposition: 'defer', reason: 'flood:burst' }
```

Pass `now: () => clock` to both factories to drive time from the test instead of the wall clock. `createFocusFirewall({ config })` adds the per-class rates on top; its `observe()` returns kehto's `EvaluateResult`.

Scenarios worth writing for your own applet:

1. Mount hidden, then show: everything your applet queued while hidden arrives in order and your UI settles.
2. Lose focus mid-operation: your publish still completes, later; nothing is dropped and nothing is retried twice.
3. Hit `rate:*` on purpose: your applet shows the user something useful instead of a stack trace.
4. Be declined: require nothing you cannot explain in the one line the consent prompt shows.
5. New build, old user: your applet's new hash has no grants. Make the first run after an update as good as the first run ever.

## Run it in kernl

Follow [Run the shell](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/run-the-shell.md), publish your applet with the napplet tooling to a relay the shell reads, and open it by address. The grants panel shows you exactly which prompt your `requires` produced and every guard event your applet triggered, with its reason. That panel is the fastest feedback you will get on posture.

## Related

- [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md)
- [Identity and grants](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/identity-and-grants.md)
- [Spec conformance](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md)

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/run-the-shell.md -->

# Run the shell

This tutorial takes you from a clone to an applet running in a window, signed in with your own account, and shows the `Kernl` calls behind each step. It takes about ten minutes.

> **Alpha**
>
> The shell runs, but it is a first draft. Expect rough edges in the UI and read [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md) for what is not there yet.

## Prerequisites

- Node 22 or newer and pnpm 10. The repository pins `pnpm@10.24.0` through `packageManager`; `corepack enable` picks it up.
- A way to sign: a browser extension that speaks NIP-07, a remote signer that speaks NIP-46, or nothing, in which case the shell creates a local account protected by a password. kernl never asks for a private key directly and never stores one in plaintext.
- The address of an applet to open. The [napplet.run app store](https://napplet.run/apps/) lists published applets with their addresses.

## 1. Clone and install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kernlize/web.git kernl
cd kernl
pnpm install
```

`pnpm install` links the four workspace packages, the docs and the app. Nothing is downloaded at runtime later; the shell's CSP would not allow it.

## 2. Start the site

```bash
pnpm site:dev
```

This runs the Astro dev server for `apps/web`. The landing site is at the root and the shell at `/app/`:

```
http://localhost:4321/app/
```

The first load shows the shell with no account. `boot.ts` has called `createKernl({ host })`, where `host` is the page's `KernlHost`: `localStorage`, the consent dialog, the notices, link confirmation and window visibility. The guard is already running in its `strict` profile and the relay tiers are `DEFAULT_RELAY_TIERS`. Add `?preview=1` to the URL to run the offline preview instead, with two sample applets and no network (D-011).

## 3. Sign in

Click *Sign in* and choose one:

- **Browser extension.** The shell wraps the extension in an applesauce `ExtensionAccount`; your key stays in the extension.
- **Remote signer.** Paste a `bunker://` address, or show the pairing code to your signer app. Either way the shell holds a `NostrConnectAccount` over an applesauce `NostrConnectSigner` that talks through the shell's own `RelayPool`.
- **Read-only.** Paste a public key. The session is `readOnly`, applets see the identity, and every write is refused because `createAuthHooks` returns no signer.
- **Create a local account.** Choose a password. The shell generates a key inside an applesauce `PasswordSigner` and persists it as a `PasswordAccount`, whose serialised form is NIP-49 encrypted. A plaintext-key account is refused by `KernlAccountManager` with `denied:plaintext-key-persistence`.

Each path ends in `kernl.login(account)`, which adds the account to the `AccountManager` if it is new, makes it active and emits a `Session` on `kernl.session$`. Accounts and the active choice persist at `kernl:accounts:v1` and `kernl:active-account:v1`, so the next load signs you in again (a password account asks to be unlocked). Nothing is fetched at sign-in: profile, follows and relay list are loaded from the `discovery` tier the first time an applet or the shell asks for them.

```ts
import { createKernl, type KernlHost } from '@kernl/core';
import type { IAccount } from 'applesauce-accounts';

declare const host: KernlHost;
declare const account: IAccount;

const kernl = createKernl({ host, relays: { apps: ['wss://relay.napplet.soy'] } });

const session = await kernl.login(account);
session.readOnly; // true for a ReadonlyAccount; writes are then refused
```

## 4. Open an applet by address

Click *Open* and paste an address. `kernl.decodePointer` accepts an `naddr1…`, an `nevent1…` or `note1…`, a bare 64-hex event id, any of those behind `nostr:`, and a coordinate in either `<pubkey>:<kind>:<identifier>` or `<kind>:<pubkey>:<identifier>` order. Anything else is `invalid:pointer`.

`kernl.resolve(pointer)` fetches the manifest from the pointer's relay hints plus the `apps` tier, verifies its signature, fetches the artifact bytes by hash and verifies them. Nothing runs before verification passes; a tampered artifact is `invalid:blob-hash-mismatch`, a missing one `unavailable:blob`, a manifest nobody serves `unavailable:manifest`. When it passes, the launcher shows the `AppletSummary`: title, publisher, the identity (`dTag` and the hash of the build you are about to run), and the domains it `requires` and lists as `optional`, each as a switch.

The baseline domains (`shell`, `inc`, `theme`, `identity`, `storage`) are always on and cannot be switched off. Every other switch starts where this identity's grants already are, which on a first run is off; a required domain is marked "the applet says it needs this", and a warning names the required domains still off and says you can run anyway. Click *Run*. The launcher calls `kernl.grants.allowDomain` for each switch you turned on and `kernl.grants.revokeDomain` for each you turned off, then `kernl.plan(summary)`, and opens a window for the `MountPlan`. If `plan.missingRequired` is not empty, the applet sees those domains as unavailable.

```ts
const summary = await kernl.resolve(kernl.decodePointer(`${session.pubkey}:35129:chat`));
summary.requires; // advisory, never a grant
const plan = await kernl.plan(summary);
plan.missingRequired; // required domains the user has not allowed
```

The window's iframe is mounted with `kernl.mount(plan, iframe)`: the frame gets `sandbox="allow-scripts"` and the controller-denying `allow` policy, is registered with its verified identity, has its environment frozen, is watched for a second load, and only then receives `srcdoc`. The applet sends its `hello`, which passes through the guard pipeline on its way to kehto's bridge, and `shell.init` tells it the domains it has.

## 5. Watch the guard

The desktop bar shows *Guard · strict · N*, where N counts guard events. Open it to see the profile, the eleven mitigations with the limit each one applies in the current profile (`kernl.guard.mitigations()`), and the event log (`kernl.guard.events$`). If an applet hits a limit, the log shows the window, the operation class and the reason, for example `rate:relay:publish` or `flood:quarantine`. A quarantined applet is revoked and its window removed; the notice says so.

Changing the profile here calls `kernl.guard.setProfile(profile)`, which rebuilds the guard for every window and is not remembered across reloads. [Change the guard profile](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/change-guard-profile.md) has the details and the numbers.

## 6. Grant, revoke, block

Each window has a grants panel. It lists every domain the shell offers (`kernl.grants.availableDomains()`) as a switch, with the baseline fixed on. Turning a switch on is `kernl.grants.allowDomain(identity, domain)`; off is `kernl.grants.revokeDomain(identity, domain)`. Both write kehto's ACL at once, so the applet's next call on a revoked domain is refused; the domains it was told about at mount do not change until it is opened again. *Block* is `kernl.grants.block(identity)`: the ACL denies everything and the next mount advertises `shell` alone. Closing the window is `handle.close()`, which revokes the binding and removes the frame; the grants stay, keyed by identity, for the next time you open the same build.

[Grant and revoke](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/grant-and-revoke.md) covers each call and what it changes.

## Where next

- [Grant and revoke](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/grant-and-revoke.md) for what each prompt means and what it changes.
- [Build an applet for kernl](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/tutorials/build-an-applet-for-kernl.md) if you came here to test your own applet.
- [Deploy](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/deploy.md) to publish your own instance of the shell.
